You are fixing the findings of the whole-branch review of SMA-512 pull request 2. This is ONE fix wave covering the complete findings list — not one finding at a time.

Work from: /Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-core

## Context

This pull request extracted 13 of the 19 files in `ts/apps/iam-console/lib/` into a new server-only
package `@paigasus/console-core`, and moved `iam-console` onto it, with no behaviour change. Eight
planned tasks; seven are done. Plan:
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-13-sma-512-pr2-console-core.md`. Repository conventions and measured
gotchas: `CLAUDE.md` — read it before you start, especially the Moon entries.

## Two constraints on HOW you work, both important

**1. Do not commit, and do not touch the git index.** Commit signing on this machine is currently
unavailable (1Password is locked), so nothing can be written. There is already uncommitted work in
BOTH the index (30 files, Task 6's move plus an e2e path fix) and the working tree (5 files, Task 8's
documentation). Leave your changes in the WORKING TREE, unstaged. Never run `git add`, `git commit`,
`git stash`, `git checkout --`, `git restore` or `git reset` — any of those would destroy work that
cannot be recovered. Read-only git (`git log`, `git show`, `git diff`, `git status`) is fine.

**2. Do not attempt the affected-graph re-baseline.** Finding I3 below is a whole outstanding task and
it is NOT yours. It cannot be done on a dirty tree: its method is to touch one anchor file and measure
`moon query tasks --affected --base origin/main`, and with 35 uncommitted files moon reports the union
of everything, so every measurement would be wrong while looking right. Do not edit
`ci/affected-graph/run.sh`.

## The findings to fix

### I1 (Important) — the new package declares no `deps: ['contracts:generate']`

`ts/packages/paigasus-console-core/moon.yml` has no `deps:` on `build`, `typecheck` or `test`. All
three read `ts/packages/paigasus-proto/src/generated/**`: `testing/fake-iam.ts` imports
`@paigasus/proto` and `@paigasus/proto/iam` directly and `tsconfig.json` includes `testing/**/*`, so
`build` and `typecheck` compile it; `src/iam-clients.ts` and `src/errors.ts` reach the same tree
through `@paigasus/sdk`; and `test` loads `testing/fake-iam.ts` at run time.

`contracts:generate` runs `buf generate` with `clean: true`. It DELETES that tree and restores it only
at the end of an ~11 second run, so a concurrent task can compile against a missing tree.
`ts/packages/paigasus-discovery/moon.yml` records the measured CI failure this caused (a `TS2307`),
and `ts/apps/iam-console/moon.yml` carries the same `deps` line for the same reason. Read both before
you edit, and follow their shape.

`dependsOn: paigasus-proto-ts` does NOT supply this: as `ts/packages/paigasus-sdk/moon.yml` records,
`dependsOn` schedules a project sync, never an upstream TASK.

Fix: add `deps: ['contracts:generate']` to `build`, `typecheck` and `test` in the new package's
`moon.yml`, and extend that file's header comment — which currently states only two of the three
rules — to name the ordering rule as well. Check whether any OTHER task in that file needs it too.

### I2 (Important) — the app keeps two inputs whose only reader has left, under a false comment

`ts/apps/iam-console/moon.yml`, in `iam-console-ts:test`'s `inputs`, around lines 277-280:

```yaml
# SMA-511 D6: tests/unit/prn-tenancy.test.ts replays the kernel parity corpus and pins ROOT_PRN to
# root_prn()'s builder call. Without these, a corpus or model.rs edit serves a cached PASS.
- '/rs/crates/libs/paigasus-kernel-parity/vectors/**/*'
- '/rs/crates/libs/paigasus-iam-core/src/authz/model.rs'
```

`tests/unit/prn-tenancy.test.ts` moved into the package, which now declares the same two inputs
correctly. Nothing under `ts/apps/iam-console/` reads the parity vectors or `model.rs` any more —
verify that yourself before deleting, with a grep, and say what you found.

Two effects today: the comment states a fact that is no longer true, and a Rust parity edit runs a
full `next build` plus the Tailwind guard plus 211 app tests for nothing. `repo:input-liveness` cannot
report it, because the globs still match tracked files and that gate scans `repo:*` tasks only.

Fix: delete both input lines and their comment from the app's `moon.yml`. Check whether the app's
OTHER tasks (`build`, `typecheck`, `test-e2e`) carry the same two lines, and treat each on the same
test — does anything that task compiles or runs still read those files?

### I4 (Important) — harden the `lib/auth.ts` / `lib/console.ts` module cycle

`ts/apps/iam-console/lib/console.ts:13` reads the imported `authRuntime` BINDING at module scope,
inside the `createConsoleRuntime(...)` argument. That is safe only because `authRuntime` is a hoisted
`export function` declaration. A comment now records that, but a comment is weak here for a measured
reason this repository already knows: CLAUDE.md records that Next gives a route handler and a page
SEPARATE module graphs (SMA-511), so both entry orders really occur in production. If someone converts
`authRuntime` to `export const authRuntime = () => ...`, one layer keeps working and the other throws a
TDZ `ReferenceError` at module load — the same split-by-layer failure shape that caused the SMA-511
login loop, and no unit test would see it.

Fix: in `ts/apps/iam-console/lib/console.ts`, pass `authRuntime: () => authRuntime()` instead of
passing the binding directly. The identifier then resolves at CALL time, not at module-evaluation
time, which removes the hazard for every declaration form. Keep a comment, but change what it says —
it should now record that the wrapper is what makes the cycle safe, not the declaration form. Update
the comment at `ts/apps/iam-console/lib/auth.ts` (around lines 20-24) to match, rather than leaving two
comments that disagree.
Check the type still fits: `createConsoleRuntime` takes `authRuntime: () => Promise<AuthRuntime>`.

### M1 (Minor) — stale `lib/...` references inside the moved package

Task 8 updated `CLAUDE.md`, both READMEs and the spec, but not the in-file comments. The reviewer
listed these; verify each against the file before editing, because a line number may have moved:
`src/correlation.ts:4,25`; `src/authorize.ts:17`; `src/principal-prn.ts:6,7`; `src/principal.ts:21,23,24`;
`src/principal-resolver.ts:27,71`; `src/scopes.ts:99,124`; `src/errors.ts:66` (it says `iam.ts`'s
`iamClientsForAction`; that file is gone and the text now lives in `runtime.ts`);
`tests/unit/authorize.test.ts:46,71`; `tests/unit/correlation.test.ts:3`;
`tests/integration/principal.test.ts:52,169,180`. Also `tests/integration/discovery.test.ts:11` says
"the runtime-ports seam", which this branch deleted, and `tests/support/msw.ts:14` says "deferred to
task 6", which has happened.

Do a `grep -n "lib/" ts/packages/paigasus-console-core/` sweep of your own rather than working only
from that list — the reviewer says it finds all of them, so confirm it does. Fix the paths and the
statements; do not rewrite comments whose content is still correct.

### M2 (Minor) — three stale user-facing doc lines

- `ts/apps/iam-console/README.md:11` — "`mayI()` (`lib/authorize.ts`)".
- `ts/apps/iam-console/README.md:52` — "an in-process fake IAM (`tests/support/fake-iam.ts`)".
- `CLAUDE.md` around lines 1025-1027 — the `forbidden()` bullet still says `lib/iam.ts` sends the
  correlation header and `lib/correlation.ts` holds `FORBIDDEN_VIEW_CORRELATION`. Its neighbours were
  corrected; this one was missed.

**Two hazards in `CLAUDE.md`, both measured and both able to red CI.** The file contains a
marker-delimited `moon ci` command between `<!-- ci-targets:begin -->` and `<!-- ci-targets:end -->`; a
SECOND copy of either marker anywhere in the file — even inside backticks in prose — makes the count 2
and reds `repo:affected-smoke`. Do not add, move, quote or duplicate those markers and do not change
the command between them. The file also has a `<!-- moon-diagnosis:begin -->` / `:end -->` block and a
rule that any file naming `ciReport.json` needs a `<!-- moon-diagnosis:ok -->` marker — do not add a
mention of `ciReport.json`.

### M7 (Minor) — `testcontainers` is an unused devDependency of the new package

The reviewer checked every declared dependency and found `testcontainers` in no file of
`ts/packages/paigasus-console-core/`. It was copied from a sibling manifest. Verify that yourself with
a grep, and if it holds, remove it from `package.json`. Do NOT run `pnpm install` to regenerate the
lockfile unless removing it actually requires a lockfile change — if it does, run
`pnpm -C ts install --lockfile-only` and say so; the lockfile must stay consistent either way.
While you are there, check the other declared dependencies the same way and report any other that
nothing imports. Do not remove `@paigasus/proto`, `@connectrpc/connect-node` or `jose` — the reviewer
verified `testing/` needs all three.

## Findings you must NOT act on

Deliberately deferred by the controller: the `src/global.d.ts` global `HeadersInit` declaration (it
works and its two failure modes are documented in the file); the package `typecheck` task's inputs not
covering `tests/**/*` (predates this branch and affects every `ts` package); the duplicated
`IDS`/`callsSince()` test fixtures; the two hard-coded `'__Host-pgs_sid'` literals in
`tests/unit/action-session.test.ts`; adding a `./correlation-header` package subpath; making `callIam`
take the injected logger; and adding a client-boundary build-guard fixture for
`@paigasus/console-core`. Leave every one of those alone.

## Verification

Run all of these and report the real output:
`moon run paigasus-console-core-ts:test`, `moon run paigasus-console-core-ts:typecheck`,
`moon run iam-console-ts:test`, `moon run iam-console-ts:typecheck`, `moon run iam-console-ts:build`,
`moon run paigasus-next-config-ts:test`, `moon run ts:lint`, `moon run ts:fmt`.
Prefix with `export PATH="$HOME/.proto/shims:$HOME/.proto/bin:$PATH"`.

Baselines measured by the controller before this wave: `iam-console-ts:test` 32 files / 211 tests plus
the tailwind-source guard; `paigasus-console-core-ts:test` 11 files / 124 tests;
`paigasus-next-config-ts:test` 204 tests; `ts:lint` and `ts:fmt` clean. None of your changes should
move a test count — say so if one does and why.

I1 changes task ordering, so re-run `moon run paigasus-console-core-ts:build` too and confirm the
`contracts:generate` dependency actually schedules. If an external BSR rate limit makes
`contracts:generate` fail, that is unrelated to your change: say so plainly, name exactly which
evidence you could and could not obtain, and never leave a generated file deleted.

## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

Do all of this work yourself. Never spawn a subagent, and never spawn a reviewer.

## Report

Write your report to
`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-core/.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-13-sma-512-pr2-console-core/final-fix-report.md`.
Include, each as its own line: what you changed for each of I1, I2, I4, M1, M2 and M7; the grep
evidence for I2 and M7; whether the `CLAUDE.md` markers still appear exactly twice each (one begin, one
end) and the command between the ci-targets markers is unchanged; every verification command with its
real result; and confirmation that you staged and committed nothing.

Then reply with ONLY (under 15 lines):
- **Status:** DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT
- Files changed (paths only)
- One-line test summary
- Your concerns, if any
- The report file path

# Model routing

Default subagents to the cheapest tier that can do the job. Pass `model`
explicitly on every Agent call — an unqualified spawn inherits the coordinator's
tier, which is usually the most expensive one.

- **Searches and lookups → the `Explore` agent**, never `general-purpose`:
  "where does X live", "which crates depend on Y", "find every call site".
  `general-purpose` carries full tool access at the coordinator's tier.
- **Haiku** for mechanical, low-judgment work: CI failure triage (parsing
  `ciReport.json`, finding which target went red), lockfile and dependency
  forensics, format/header/SPDX sweeps, PR review-thread enumeration, log and
  test-output summarization.
- **Sonnet** for single-domain analysis needing judgment but not synthesis.
- **Opus** only where a wrong answer is expensive: adversarial review, plan
  writing, cross-cutting synthesis, and CI meta-machinery.
- If you already know the file path, `Read` it. Don't spawn an agent to find
  something you can open directly.

** Use subagents whenever possible.** This explicitely overrules any contrary previous instructions.

# Write in Simplified Technical English

Write all user-facing text in **ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English**. This
applies to every message, not only to documentation, and in every project.

Sven asked for this directly on 2026-08-10. He did not give a reason, so do not
assume one, and do not write a reason into any document as if he had stated it.

- Use approved words from the STE dictionary. One word has one meaning and one
  part of speech. Use "use", not "leverage" or "utilize". Use "start", not "kick
  off". Use "make", not "spin up".
- Keep sentences short. Maximum 20 words for an instruction. Maximum 25 words for
  a description. Put one idea in one sentence.
- Use the active voice. Write "the test failed", not "a failure was seen".
- Use simple tenses. Prefer the present tense and the simple past.
- Do not use idiom, metaphor, irony or humour. Do not write "the loop caught me"
  or "this bit us". Write what happened.
- Keep articles ("the", "a") in place. Do not drop them to save words.
- Use a maximum of six sentences in a paragraph.

# paigasus-core

Public, Apache-2.0 polyglot monorepo for Paigasus, orchestrated by Moon. Four workspaces:
`contracts/` (protobuf + buf), `rs/` (Cargo: libs/bindings/services), `py/` (uv),
`ts/` (pnpm). **Status: bootstrapping** — workspaces are scaffolded issue-by-issue, so a
dir may hold only a README until its setup issue lands.

## Setup & commands

Tooling runs through [Moon](https://moonrepo.dev), pinned via proto in `.prototools`.
First-time setup: see [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md#local-development) (`proto install` → `moon`).

- `moon ci :build` / `moon ci :test` — affected build/test graph. **Moon 2.x needs explicit
  targets**; bare `moon ci` errors in non-TTY.
- Task output style is set in `.moon/tasks.yml` (`taskOptions.outputStyle`,
  currently `buffer-only-failure`). Moon 2.5.3 still has no per-invocation CLI flag
  for it (re-checked on the 2.5.3 bump, SMA-595); to stream a specific task locally, set
  `options.outputStyle: 'stream'` on the task definition. Note moon 2.4.3 changed the
  setting to apply only to TRANSITIVE targets, not the primary one you name.
- Rust (in `rs/`): `cargo build --workspace`, `cargo fmt --check`,
  `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`, `cargo nextest run --workspace`.

## Architecture

- `contracts/` — proto source of truth; buf generates Rust/Py/TS bindings (ADR-0004).
- `rs/crates/{libs,bindings,services}/` — `libs` = pure crates (e.g. `paigasus-kernel`),
  `bindings` = FFI shims (PyO3/napi/wasm), `services` = binaries. Service crates follow
  hexagonal architecture; libs/bindings do not.
- Cross-language behavior lives once in `paigasus-kernel` (Rust), bound to Py/Node/WASM —
  never reimplemented per language (ADR-0005).

## Conventions

- Every source file opens with an SPDX header: `// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0`
  (`#` for Python).
- Branches: `feature/sma-NNN-<slug>` off `main` (NOT the old `sven/...` form).
- Conventional commits with a workspace scope: `feat(rs): …`, `fix(contracts): …`.
- Rust crates use **edition 2024 + rust-version 1.95**, even when an issue's AC says 2021.
- Significant choices get a Notion ADR before code; conventions live in the Notion
  Development Guidelines (both linked from CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Gotchas

- Moon is 2.5.3 and proto is 0.61.1 (SMA-595): `vcs.client` (not `manager`), `codeowners.sync`
  (not `syncOnRun`), Python/uv toolchains keyed `unstable_python` + a separate `unstable_uv`.
  The two pins are **coupled**: moon 2.5.3's Python toolchain plugin requires proto >= 0.60.0,
  and moon reads the proto CLI at the fixed path `~/.proto/bin/proto` — neither `PATH` order nor
  the `.prototools` pin overrides that, so a moon bump can hard-fail with
  `proto::tool::minimum_version_requirement` until the local proto BINARY moves. `proto upgrade`
  reports the target version and then no-ops inside an agent session; upgrade it from a normal
  shell, or set `PROTO_HOME` to an isolated root and `proto install` into it.
- `proto` prints **NDJSON on stdout** when it detects an agent environment (`AI_AGENT`,
  `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`), including a `Detected an AI agent environment…`
  preamble line. That breaks any captured `$(proto <subcommand> …)`: the variable becomes a JSON
  blob, not a path, and the `||` fallbacks never fire because proto **exits 0** — it succeeded, it
  just answered in a different language. It is a property of proto's reporter, not of `proto bin`.
  **Pass `--reporter text`** (or `PROTO_REPORTER=text`) on any proto call whose stdout you capture;
  `ci/release-parity/ecosystems/release-plz.sh` is the worked example, and it also asserts
  `[ -x ]` on the result so a future regression fails at the assignment rather than 87 lines later
  (SMA-596). This is NOT new in proto 0.61.1; 0.58.1 behaves identically (measured both, SMA-595).
  A proto-**shimmed** tool (`uv`, `node`, `release-plz`) was recorded here as a different case —
  the shim execs the tool, so captured stdout is the tool's — "measured for the two cases below,
  not proven generally". **That carve-out is now DISPROVEN and must not be relied on** (SMA-609).
  A captured `uv` shim call leaked the preamble into `$(...)` twice on merged `main`: once from
  `repo:ruff-ci`'s binary resolver, once from `repo:actionlint` check 10's `--fixture-count`. Both
  died with a JSON blob where a path or an integer belonged. It is INTERMITTENT — the same command
  succeeds on the next run — so a green does not clear a captured shim call. Directly measured on
  the shim: the default reporter yields `{"type":"message",…}` on stdout, `PROTO_REPORTER=text`
  yields none. Every gate script that captures shim output therefore **exports
  `PROTO_REPORTER=text` once at the top** (`ci/actionlint/`, `ci/ruff/`, `ci/release-plan/`,
  `ci/release-parity/`), rather than prefixing each call site, so a future capture inherits it.
  The two binary resolvers additionally pipe through `tail -n1`; note that alone is NOT
  sufficient — on the multi-line NDJSON error the last line is still JSON, and what preserves
  fail-closed there is the `[ -x ]` assertion, not the tail.
  **Scope, corrected.** Only `repo:release-parity` was ever affected — NOT all three.
  `ci/release-parity/run.sh` sources exactly ONE ecosystem module per invocation, and only
  `release-plz.sh` invoked the proto CLI; `-py` resolves through `uv run` and `-ts` through `node`,
  and both were measured green in the same agent session that showed `release-parity` aborting.
  The earlier claim here that all three abort was a regression against SMA-530's own spec, which
  had the scope right. The `unset AI_AGENT CLAUDECODE CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` workaround is **no
  longer needed for these gates**; it may still matter for other proto oddities (see the entry
  above). **Residual:** nothing gates this. A new captured proto call written the broken way reds
  nothing (SMA-596 D4) — this bullet is the only control.
  Both ecosystem modules now resolve their tool with **no fallback** and assert `[ -x ]`, exiting 2
  with the harness's own `infrastructure error (rc=2)` classifier in the message — the module is
  sourced by `run.sh`, so an exit fires during the source and `run.sh` never reaches its own abort
  lines. That classifier is what keeps such a failure greppable.
- `repo:affected-smoke` has aborted **twice**, both times under a concurrent `moon ci` on 2.5.3,
  at ~2.4s against its usual 6–8s: once on SMA-595, which captured no output, and once on
  SMA-592, which captured its output. The two are matched on SYMPTOM SHAPE alone — a sub-3s abort
  under a concurrent `moon ci` — so nothing proves they are one and the same failure. Neither
  session reproduced it: four attempts on SMA-595 (warm, cold `.moon/cache`, cold `MOON_HOME`, and
  cold `rs/target` with cargo compiling alongside), and three more on SMA-592. An inherited
  `MOON_BASE` was tested and ruled out (the gate passes with it set). The gate is otherwise green
  everywhere. If you see a sub-3s `affected-smoke` failure, capture the full task output before
  re-running, because a re-run passes and destroys the evidence.
  (SMA-597 measured the mechanism: it is OVERWRITE, not discard. A passing re-run rewrites
  `stdout.log`, truncates `stderr.log`, rewrites `lastRun.json` and flips the `ciReport.json` row
  to `passed`. See the diagnosis procedure entry below.)
  **The mechanism below is measured on the ONE session that captured output (SMA-592), not on
  both.** In that occurrence the failure is an infrastructure ABORT, not a red verdict: the gate's
  own nested `moon query projects` dies with `Error: proto-shim:
  Failed to execute proto for the shimmed command: Permission denied (os error 13)`, writes
  nothing to stdout, and the reader then raises `JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column
  1`, so `run.sh` prints `FATAL [contracts->proto]: moon query failed` and
  `== affected-graph guard ABORTED: infrastructure error (rc=2) ==`. So the proximate cause THERE
  is the **proto shim failing to exec `proto` with EACCES** while a `moon ci` runs concurrently —
  why the shim is briefly non-executable is still unknown, and SMA-595's four hypotheses above
  stay ruled out.
  Two consequences. The gate FAILS SAFE — rc=2 is distinct from rc=1, and it never reports a false
  green. And the `proto-shim` line is the tell, so grep the captured output for it: if that line
  is there, the failure is not about the affected graph at all, and re-running the task alone
  (`moon run repo:affected-smoke --force`) passes in the usual 6s. If it is absent, this entry
  does not explain your failure — diagnose it on its own terms.
  The NDJSON entry above is the same root tool, a different symptom; both mean a `moon`/`proto`
  call inside a gate is the fragile part of an agent-driven local run, never in CI.
- **Diagnosing an unattributed `moon ci` failure.** The procedure below is MEASURED on moon 2.5.3
  (SMA-597); re-take it on a bump. It is for **local** runs — in CI see the note at the end.
  <!-- moon-diagnosis:begin -->
  **Step 0 — capture before you re-run anything.** A re-run overwrites every artifact holding the
  evidence, and a PASSING re-run is just as destructive as another failing one: it rewrites
  `stdout.log`, truncates `stderr.log` to zero bytes, rewrites `lastRun.json`, and flips the
  action to `passed` in `ciReport.json` (all four measured). Copy `.moon/cache/ciReport.json` and
  `.moon/cache/states/<project>/<task>/` somewhere outside the repo first.

  **Step 1 — which task, what command, what exit code.**
  ```bash
  jq '.actions[] | select(.status=="failed")
      | {label, error,
         exec: (.operations[] | select(.meta.type=="task-execution") | {command, exitCode})}' \
     .moon/cache/ciReport.json
  ```
  There is **no action-level `exitCode` key** — `has("exitCode")` is `false`. The widely copied
  query projects `{label, status, exitCode}` and so reports `null` for a key moon never writes,
  which is why this file has a reputation for being empty. It is not: the real exit code and the
  full command are in `operations[]`, on the entry whose `meta.type` is `task-execution`.

  **Step 2 — why.** `cat .moon/cache/states/<project>/<task>/stdout.log` and `stderr.log`. This is
  the only place task output exists. It works for a task that never started: a missing binary
  leaves `stdout.log` empty and `stderr.log` holding `command not found` (exit 127).

  **Step 2a — prove the logs belong to this run. Mandatory.** Compare the report action's
  `finishedAt` against `lastRun.json`'s `lastRunTime`. **If they disagree, stop** — the logs are
  from a different run and pairing them with step 1's command yields a confident wrong answer.
  Two measured causes: `moon run` writes `runReport.json` and does NOT touch `ciReport.json`, so a
  `moon run` re-run desynchronises them; and a cache HIT rewrites neither, so a log can be
  arbitrarily older than the run you are looking at.

  **Step 3 — if it still does not reproduce.** `moon run <target> --force`. Note that
  `buffer-only-failure` prints a FAILING task's output but discards a PASSING one's, and that this
  re-run desynchronises the report and the logs per step 2a.

  **What cannot work:** no `--summary` level (`none`/`minimal`/`normal`/`detailed`) and no
  `outputStyle` (`stream`/`buffer`/`none`) puts stdout or stderr into `ciReport.json`; all seven
  cells are byte-identical, and a key walk over the whole failing action finds no output field at
  any depth. `--log-file` captures moon's own tracing, not a task's stdio. Do not re-litigate this.

  **In CI this procedure does not apply as written.** There is no shell and the runner is
  destroyed, so step 0 is unexecutable; and `ci.yml` restores `.moon/cache` across runs, so a
  cache-hit task's logs may be from an older commit entirely. Use the `moon-diagnostics` artifact
  that `ci.yml` uploads on failure.
  <!-- moon-diagnosis:end -->
- `cargo nextest` exits non-zero on a workspace with **no tests** — use `--no-tests=pass`.
- `.github/CODEOWNERS` is Moon-generated — don't hand-edit.
- `vcs.hooks` is intentionally empty; lefthook will own `.git/hooks` (SMA-371).
- A fresh `git worktree` starts with **no installed deps** (empty `ts/node_modules`, no
  `py/.venv`, unfetched cargo) — but lefthook's git hooks are shared across worktrees via the
  common `.git`, so `commit-msg` runs `commitlint` and **fails the commit** (`commitlint not
  found`) until deps exist. After `git worktree add`, provision the worktree before committing:
  `proto install` → `pnpm -C ts install` (installs commitlint + re-syncs hooks via its
  `prepare` step) → `uv sync` in `py/` → `cargo fetch` in `rs/`. Do **not** bypass the hook with
  `--no-verify`; install the deps.
- Never name a source file with a base name that is a **Windows reserved device name**
  (`CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1`–`COM9`, `LPT1`–`LPT9`) — `PRN.<ext>` etc. are reserved
  too, so git can't check the file out on Windows (`error: invalid path …`). The Linux-only
  `CI` gate passes; only a Windows matrix job catches it — `prebuild`'s `build win32-x64-msvc`
  and `wheels`' `wheel win-amd64`. Both DO carry a `pull_request` trigger, but a PATH-FILTERED
  one (`.moon/**`, `.prototools`, `ts/pnpm-lock.yaml`, …), so whether a PR sees the failure
  depends on what else the PR touches, not on the bad file: SMA-448 (`prn.rs` →
  `resource_name.rs`) was green on the PR and red on `main`, while SMA-511
  (`ts/apps/iam-console/lib/prn.ts` → `prn-tenancy.ts`) reddened both Windows legs on the PR
  because it also touched `.moon/**`. The rule is language-neutral: it bit a `.rs` file and a
  `.ts` file the same way. An underscore/hyphen suffix (`prn_canonical`, `prn-fields`,
  `prn-tenancy`) is fine.

  that every `T` entry still resolves to a CI-eligible task. That last half matters because
  `moon ci` exits **0** on a target that resolves to nothing (even with real targets around it), so
  a typo is otherwise a silent no-op on every PR. A gate that must stay out of `T` needs a
  `T_EXEMPT` entry with a reason — `runInCI: false` is NOT a general escape, since Moon then drops
  the task from `moon run` under `CI=true` too (see the comments in `ts/moon.yml`). `T` must also

  (`ci/affected-graph/task_inputs.py`) fails if a declared glob matches zero tracked files or a
  declared file is untracked, so moving a directory a gate keys on reds CI instead of silently
  switching that gate off. It also asserts its OWN `inputs: ['**/*']` is unchanged — narrowing it
  for cost would make it stop noticing exactly the renames it exists to catch. A genuinely dead
  input needs an `ALLOW_DEAD_INPUT` entry with a reason (SMA-553).

  `rs/deny.toml` `[licenses] exceptions` or a dev-only
  `[advisories] ignore` (Rust); an npm/pip advisory needs a version bump — a pnpm-workspace

- Moon 2.5.3's Rust toolchain resolves `path = "…"` Cargo deps into the project graph **automatically**
  (`moon query projects` labels them `source=implicit`), but does **not** resolve `workspace = true`
  inheritance. So a `{ workspace = true }` in-tree dep — the repo's default form — **must** be
  hand-declared in `dependsOn`, while a `path` dep needs nothing. This is why the drift was scattered
  rather than systematic, and it is the opposite of the "Cargo path deps are NOT auto-synced" claim
  that SMA-389 recorded and SMA-524 disproved. Either way the project edge alone is **not enough**:
  `dependsOn` is what `moon query projects --affected` follows, and a task-level `^:build` is what
  actually schedules the upstream's build under `moon ci --include-relations` — neither implies the
  other. `repo:affected-smoke` now asserts both generically for every crate
  (`ci/affected-graph/cargo_moon_parity.py`), so a new in-tree dep that forgets either one reds CI
  instead of silently under-building (SMA-524).
  Neither is enough on its own either: task `inputs` are the **only** thing that confers
  affectedness in Moon 2.5.3. `dependsOn` and `^:build` schedule an upstream's build but never
  **select** a downstream — a dependent runs only if independently affected. `--include-relations`
  is very nearly, but no longer entirely, inert: re-measured at the full 27-target shape on 2.5.3
  (SMA-595) it selects exactly ONE task the same command without it does not,
  `paigasus-kernel-py:build` — 44 RunTasks against 43, stable across repeated runs. On 2.3.2 the
  two sets were byte-identical (SMA-528). One added `build` is NOT a dependent closure, so the rule
  above still holds; do not read the flag as a working cascade. **Re-run that A/B on the next moon
  bump** — the delta moved once and can move again. Every Rust crate therefore
  declares its transitive upstream sources in `fileGroups.upstreams`, consumed by build/test/lint via
  `@group(upstreams)` in `.moon/tasks/rust.yml`. Omitting the group is a hard graph-load error
  (`project::unknown_file_group`) for every moon command; mis-declaring it reds
  `repo:affected-smoke`'s A6 — and **nothing else can**, because a crate's own `moon.yml` is not an
  input to its tasks, so a wrong group otherwise serves a cached PASS. `^:build` has a second job
  here: it orders `contracts:generate` before a downstream that keys on
  `paigasus-proto/src/generated/**`, so removing it as "vestigial" would make those cache keys
  nondeterministic.
- Bash tool PATH lacks the proto-managed CLIs; prefix commands with
  `export PATH="$HOME/.proto/shims:$HOME/.proto/bin:$PATH"` so moon/uv/buf/nextest resolve to
  the repo-pinned versions (shims first).
- `paigasus-iam`'s Docker-backed suites get their retry budget and container-concurrency cap from
  `rs/.config/nextest.toml` (`profile.default`), so **Moon, `moon run …:test`, and a bare
  `cargo nextest` all pick it up** — but `cargo test` does NOT, since nextest config is
  nextest-only. Don't add `--retries` to a Moon task or a doc: that recreates the
  documented-vs-executed split SMA-521 closed. A test that fails every attempt still reds; one
  that passes on a retry is reported FLAKY. The JUnit report itself is NOT on `profile.default` —
  nextest resolves a profile's report path relative to the shared workspace `target/`, so `moon
  ci`'s 15+ concurrent nextest runs would clobber a report left on `default`. It lives on a
  dedicated `[profile.iam]` instead, selected only by `paigasus-iam-rs:test`'s `args: ['--profile',
  'iam']` — CI uploads it as the `nextest-junit` artifact, but a bare `cargo nextest run -p
  paigasus-iam` writes no report at all.
- `paigasus-iam`'s **Docker-backed** suites (65 of its 69 integration binaries) skip when the
  daemon is unreachable, and that skip is deliberately quiet — nextest discards a passing test's
  stderr and Moon discards a passing task's output, so no message can surface there. What makes
  it visible is `tests/docker_preflight.rs`, a canary that FAILS when Docker is unreachable: a
  Docker-less run yields exactly one red instead of 64 silent passes (SMA-538). The policy itself
  lives once, in `tests/support/docker.rs`, and `repo:iam-docker-policy-single-site` fails if a
  new suite hand-rolls its own copy. Two env vars, both parsing `1`/`true`/`yes` (anything else,
  including `0`, is off — unlike `CI`, which is presence-based):
  `PAIGASUS_REQUIRE_DOCKER=1` turns every suite's skip into a panic, which is what a FILTERED run
  (`--test relay_pg`, `-E 'test(foo)'`) needs, since the canary is not in that filter.
  `PAIGASUS_SKIP_DOCKER=1` restores skipping everywhere including the canary — it is a
  per-invocation escape hatch for a Docker Hub rate limit or a daemon restart, **not** a
  shell-profile setting, and a `moon run` that greened under it leaves a cached PASS that replays
  after Docker returns, so follow it with `moon run … --force`. `CI` outranks both, so no
  workflow-file env var can green a CI run that tested nothing. A container that fails with a
  REACHABLE daemon is a hard failure by default — including `keycloak_e2e`'s 240s startup
  timeout, which used to be a fast local skip — though `PAIGASUS_SKIP_DOCKER=1` still downgrades
  it to a skip, since that hatch is checked before any classification happens. A stray `CI=false` still counts as "CI present" (the
  check is presence-based, not value-based) — clear it with `env -u CI cargo nextest run -p
  paigasus-iam`.
- Broad `inputs: ['**/*']` Moon tasks (e.g. `repo:actionlint`) stay cheap only because

  vocabulary, so it cannot see a code you invented and never added to
  `contracts/proto/paigasus/common/v1/error.proto`; adding the code there is what makes it
  resolvable on any consumer. Code **removal** needs no gate — both service crates carry

  crate affected. What makes it true is `@group(upstreams)` — both service crates' `test` now key on
  `paigasus-proto`'s sources, so a contracts change that regenerates them selects the test.)

## Workflow

Specs/plans live in `docs/superpowers/specs/` and `docs/superpowers/plans/` (date-prefixed,
per Linear issue). Work flows brainstorm → spec → plan → implement. Linear keys are `SMA-NNN`;
PRs auto-link to Linear by branch name (don't attach links manually).

# Memory Index

One line per memory: enough to decide whether to open it. The detail lives in the topic file.

## Project shape & process

- [Frontend architecture scoped in Notion](paigasus-frontend-architecture-scoped.md) — multi-zone BFF console lives in Notion, NOT the repo; ADR-0017–0021 Accepted and Better Auth rejected, don't re-litigate; the ADR index table has no gate and drifts
- [audit_log partitioning + observability layout](sma-446-remaining-observability.md) — `audit_log` is LIST→RANGE partitioned with in-app retention (the "plain table" note is obsolete); metrics live in `paigasus-observability` + `ops/observability/`
- [main strict checks × dependabot](paigasus-main-strict-checks-dependabot.md) — main needs `moon ci` with strict up-to-date branches, so sequential merges block the next PR; use the update-branch API once you've pushed to a dependabot branch
- [paigasus commit signing via 1Password](paigasus-commit-signing-1password.md) — SSH-signed via op-ssh-sign; "failed to fill whole buffer" = 1Password locked; GitHub-API fallback and which API produces signed commits
- [commitlint body #NNN footer gotcha](paigasus-commitlint-body-hash-footer-gotcha.md) — a `#NNN` or `token: value` line in the BODY fails `footer-leading-blank`, and the local hook can pass while CI fails

## Agents, sessions & worktrees

- [Concurrent session branch clash](paigasus-concurrent-session-branch-clash.md) — two sessions in one checkout interleave commits silently; detect with ListAgents, isolate with a worktree, never `checkout`/`branch -f` under a busy peer
- [Subagent worktree pinned cwd](subagent-worktree-pinned-cwd.md) — subagents run pinned to the MAIN checkout; their first action must be EnterWorktree + a branch check, or they commit to local main
- [Subagent background-job stalls](subagent-background-job-stalls.md) — implementers spawn a background job then end their turn waiting on it; dispatch foreground-only and verify with `git log` rather than trusting the report
- [EnterWorktree branch rename](enterworktree-branch-rename.md) — it mints `worktree-<name>`; rename to `feature/sma-NNN-<slug>` before the first commit or Linear auto-link breaks
- [Worktree sandbox: use a script file](worktree-sandbox-script-file-workaround.md) — in a worktree session the sandbox refuses gh/git loops, variables, awk and the perl alarm wrapper; run `/bin/bash <literal scratchpad script>` instead
- [ExitWorktree leaves the local branch](exitworktree-leaves-local-branch.md) — "discarded N commits" still leaves the branch; finish with `git branch -D`, and check `git worktree list` for peers first

## Review tooling (CodeRabbit)

- [CodeRabbit `review` is incremental](coderabbit-review-is-incremental.md) — zero threads means "nothing new", not "clean"; only `full review` forces a real pass. **How to tell all four zero-thread states apart** — including a clean pass that files NO review object, and why the refusal's BODY not its latency is the discriminator
- [CodeRabbit-loop in-progress detector](coderabbit-loop-inprogress-detector.md) — the skill's "come back in a few minutes" grep misses CR's other in-progress wordings; nitpicks hide in the review BODY, not reviewThreads
- [CodeRabbit rate-limit re-trigger is futile](coderabbit-rate-limit-retrigger-futile.md) — a Fair-Usage refusal is a ~393-byte body arriving as an ISSUE COMMENT; only a new push or billing gets a review
- [CodeRabbit CLI last-commit gap](coderabbit-cli-last-commit-gap.md) — a 2-pass local review never covers the fix commit it produced; one more pass found five further findings

## Gate design & proving assertions bite

- [Fixtures inherit the implementer's assumption](fixtures-inherit-the-implementer-assumption.md) — nine review passes missed a case-sensitive `content-type` check because every fixture used lowercase; vary externally-supplied strings by case, parameters and whitespace
- [Fix scope hides the same defect](fix-scope-hides-the-same-defect.md) — one bug survived three plausible scopes ("no chain here", "fix what the review named", "change nothing beyond this file"); put the rule on the helper's contract, then audit every call site
- [Guard-the-guard: pin production call sites](guard-the-guard-production-call-sites.md) — a check's own CALL SITE is what goes unguarded; fixture tables exercise the verdict function, never its invocation
- [Prometheus `# TYPE` vacuous assertions](prometheus-type-line-vacuous-assertion.md) — `contains()` on a TYPE line passes with the increment DELETED; parse a number instead. Also: a metric's prose lives in 3 unlinked places
- [Prometheus new-counter first-sample trap](prometheus-new-counter-first-sample-trap.md) — a series appears already at 1, so `increase()` can never fire on the first occurrence; prime at zero
- [promtool gate semantics](promtool-gate-semantics.md) — `check config` reads ZERO rule files, so it proves nothing about rules loading; always add a control series
- [errexit swallows nested exit codes](errexit-swallows-nested-exit-codes.md) — `foo || ec=$?` cannot see an `exit 2` raised inside a `$( )`, so a rc1-vs-rc2 negative control is silently inoperative
- [Mutation restore discards the fix](mutation-restore-discards-the-fix.md) — `git checkout --` also reverts the UNCOMMITTED fix under test; restore by deleting a marked insert
- [Re-run a mutation battery whole](mutation-battery-rerun-whole.md) — after any fix re-run every mutation; a fixture in a COMMENT went inert when a later fix stripped comments. Time out the harness
- [BSD vs GNU grep on directories](bsd-gnu-grep-directory-divergence.md) — a directory passed to `grep -c` is not a portable read failure: BSD errors, GNU prints `0`; passes on macOS, reds Linux CI
- [repo gates: dependency waivers](paigasus-repo-gates-vs-per-project-tasks.md) — new deps may need a deny.toml exception, a dev-only advisory ignore, or a temporary cargo-machete allowlist

- [moon ci affected model](moon-ci-affected-model.md) — changed-files-only by default; downstream needs `--include-relations` + task-level `^:build`. Dirs with no moon.yml belong only to root `repo`

- [Moon project id stack suffix](moon-project-id-stack-suffix.md) — ids collide across stacks; suffix `-py` / `-rs`
- [Moon layer field not type](moon-layer-field-not-type.md) — the project field is `layer:`, not `type:`
- [Moon/proto PATH in non-interactive shells](moon-proto-path-noninteractive.md) — shims FIRST or you get the global pin; the Bash tool runs zsh, and macOS has no `timeout`
- [moon .prototools runtime tool pins](moon-prototools-runtime-tool-pins.md) — pin node/pnpm/uv in `.prototools`, not only `.moon/toolchains.yml`, or fresh CI fails `proto::detect::failed`
- [proto-pin cargo CLIs](proto-pin-cargo-clis.md) — add cargo-deny/machete-style gates via a proto plugin, not `rust.bins`; host on root `repo`, toolchain:system
- [proto TOML schema arch is global-only](proto-toml-schema-arch-global-only.md) — vendored plugin TOMLs remap `{arch}` globally only; the per-OS fix is upstream
- [proto does not shim npm](proto-does-not-shim-npm.md) — `~/.proto/shims/` has `node` but NOT `npm`, so a bare `npm` in CI is the runner image's

- [macOS bash 5.3.15 here-string deadlock](macos-bash-535-herestring-deadlock.md) — THIS machine hangs forever on `while read` fed by a `<<<` over ~512 bytes; hangs `affected-smoke`/`actionlint` locally while CI stays green. Never read the hang as a gate failure
- [affected-smoke hang: use /bin/bash](affected-smoke-hang-fixed-by-system-bash.md) — the deadlock is bash-5.3.15-specific; macOS's system bash 3.2 runs the whole affected-graph suite green in under a minute
- [CI disk exhaustion from large Rust deps](paigasus-ci-disk-large-rust-deps.md) — big dep trees overflow the ~14GB runner disk mid-link; fix with CI-only `line-tables-only` debug + a versioned cache key
- [actions/cache skips save on exact key hit](actions-cache-key-hit-skips-save.md) — widening a cached job without changing the key means the output is never saved, and the verification run hides it
- [Cargo stale build after a restore](cargo-stale-build-after-restore.md) — `mv file.bak file` rolls mtime BACKWARDS so cargo reuses the binary built from your temporary edit; `touch` or revert via Edit
- [Rust fmt drift after an identifier rename](rust-fmt-drift-after-identifier-rename.md) — a longer identifier reflows past max_width; clippy stays clean and `cargo fmt --check` reds
- [Rust workspace warnings=deny staging trap](rust-workspace-warnings-deny-staging-trap.md) — dead code is a hard COMPILE error, so "add now, wire later" plan staging breaks the package
- [ts:fmt Prettier gate is separate](paigasus-ts-fmt-prettier-gate.md) — its own whole-tree CI gate, decoupled from `ts:lint`/tsc; run it after touching any ts file
- [pnpm minimum-release-age](pnpm-minimum-release-age.md) — pnpm 11's 24h default fails CI on same-day npm releases

## Dependabot & lockfiles

- [dependabot pnpm catalog corruption](dependabot-pnpm-catalog-corruption.md) — npm PRs drop a package from `catalogs.default` and rewrite its specifier off `catalog:`; hides behind the release-age check
- [dependency-graph uv-member warnings](paigasus-dependency-graph-uv-member-warnings.md) — benign: auto-discovered graph jobs failing to resolve uv workspace members standalone
- [uv constraint for a transitive CVE](uv-constraint-for-transitive-cve.md) — a group bump can DOWNGRADE a transitive dep into a CVE; use `[tool.uv] constraint-dependencies`, never an osv waiver

## Contracts, FFI & codegen

- [proto buf-format + moon ci silent-fail diagnosis](paigasus-proto-buf-format-ci-diagnosis.md) — editing a `.proto` needs `buf format -w` or `contracts:fmt` reds SILENTLY; `contracts:generate` can serve STALE cache
- [FFI binding pattern (maturin + napi + wasm)](paigasus-uv-maturin-binding-pattern.md) — the three-binding layout plus freshness traps; wasm-pack destructively cleans `--out-dir`; vitest forces the `node` condition
- [kernel FFI surface gotchas](paigasus-kernel-ffi-surface.md) — doc comments churn committed glue; use f64 not u64 at the boundary; uuid pulls getrandom and breaks wasm

- [uv_build license-files gotcha](paigasus-uv-build-license-files.md) — uv_build doesn't auto-glob license files, so a PyPI wheel ships no licence text

## Release & publishing

- [crates.io Trusted Publishing needs an existing crate](cratesio-trusted-publishing-needs-existing-crate.md) — a trusted publisher can only be created AFTER a manual first publish, so an OIDC-only job cannot do a first publish. npm same; PyPI differs
- [cargo publish embeds .cargo_vcs_info.json](cargo-publish-vcs-info-seed.md) — from ANY git tree, and `--allow-dirty` keeps it; release-plz reads that sha1 as its changelog boundary

## Async & runtime

- [tokio select! poll-arm starvation](tokio-select-poll-arm-starvation.md) — a relative `sleep` rebuilt inside `select!` restarts on every other arm firing; use an absolute deadline, and order the arms
- [Docker-gated suites silently skip](paigasus-docker-gated-suites-silent-skip.md) — the suites are genuinely FLAKY under parallel load; baseline on unmodified origin/main before blaming your diff

# paigasus-core

Public, Apache-2.0 polyglot monorepo for Paigasus, orchestrated by Moon. Four workspaces:
`contracts/` (protobuf + buf), `rs/` (Cargo: libs/bindings/services), `py/` (uv),
`ts/` (pnpm). **Status: bootstrapping** — workspaces are scaffolded issue-by-issue, so a
dir may hold only a README until its setup issue lands.

## Setup & commands

Tooling runs through [Moon](https://moonrepo.dev), pinned via proto in `.prototools`.
First-time setup: see [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md#local-development) (`proto install` → `moon`).

- `moon ci :build` / `moon ci :test` — affected build/test graph. **Moon 2.x needs explicit
  targets**; bare `moon ci` errors in non-TTY.
- Task output style is set in `.moon/tasks.yml` (`taskOptions.outputStyle`,
  currently `buffer-only-failure`). Moon 2.5.3 still has no per-invocation CLI flag
  for it (re-checked on the 2.5.3 bump, SMA-595); to stream a specific task locally, set
  `options.outputStyle: 'stream'` on the task definition. Note moon 2.4.3 changed the
  setting to apply only to TRANSITIVE targets, not the primary one you name.
- Rust (in `rs/`): `cargo build --workspace`, `cargo fmt --check`,
  `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`, `cargo nextest run --workspace`.

## Architecture

- `contracts/` — proto source of truth; buf generates Rust/Py/TS bindings (ADR-0004).
- `rs/crates/{libs,bindings,services}/` — `libs` = pure crates (e.g. `paigasus-kernel`),
  `bindings` = FFI shims (PyO3/napi/wasm), `services` = binaries. Service crates follow
  hexagonal architecture; libs/bindings do not.
- Cross-language behavior lives once in `paigasus-kernel` (Rust), bound to Py/Node/WASM —
  never reimplemented per language (ADR-0005).

## Conventions

- Every source file opens with an SPDX header: `// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0`
  (`#` for Python).
- Branches: `feature/sma-NNN-<slug>` off `main` (NOT the old `sven/...` form).
- Conventional commits with a workspace scope: `feat(rs): …`, `fix(contracts): …`.
- Rust crates use **edition 2024 + rust-version 1.95**, even when an issue's AC says 2021.
- Significant choices get a Notion ADR before code; conventions live in the Notion
  Development Guidelines (both linked from CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Gotchas

- Moon is 2.5.3 and proto is 0.61.1 (SMA-595): `vcs.client` (not `manager`), `codeowners.sync`
  (not `syncOnRun`), Python/uv toolchains keyed `unstable_python` + a separate `unstable_uv`.
  The two pins are **coupled**: moon 2.5.3's Python toolchain plugin requires proto >= 0.60.0,
  and moon reads the proto CLI at the fixed path `~/.proto/bin/proto` — neither `PATH` order nor
  the `.prototools` pin overrides that, so a moon bump can hard-fail with
  `proto::tool::minimum_version_requirement` until the local proto BINARY moves. `proto upgrade`
  reports the target version and then no-ops inside an agent session; upgrade it from a normal
  shell, or set `PROTO_HOME` to an isolated root and `proto install` into it.
- `proto` prints **NDJSON on stdout** when it detects an agent environment (`AI_AGENT`,
  `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`), including a `Detected an AI agent environment…`
  preamble line. That breaks any captured `$(proto <subcommand> …)`: the variable becomes a JSON
  blob, not a path, and the `||` fallbacks never fire because proto **exits 0** — it succeeded, it
  just answered in a different language. It is a property of proto's reporter, not of `proto bin`.
  **Pass `--reporter text`** (or `PROTO_REPORTER=text`) on any proto call whose stdout you capture;
  `ci/release-parity/ecosystems/release-plz.sh` is the worked example, and it also asserts
  `[ -x ]` on the result so a future regression fails at the assignment rather than 87 lines later
  (SMA-596). This is NOT new in proto 0.61.1; 0.58.1 behaves identically (measured both, SMA-595).
  A proto-**shimmed** tool (`uv`, `node`, `release-plz`) was recorded here as a different case —
  the shim execs the tool, so captured stdout is the tool's — "measured for the two cases below,
  not proven generally". **That carve-out is now DISPROVEN and must not be relied on** (SMA-609).
  A captured `uv` shim call leaked the preamble into `$(...)` twice on merged `main`: once from
  `repo:ruff-ci`'s binary resolver, once from `repo:actionlint` check 10's `--fixture-count`. Both
  died with a JSON blob where a path or an integer belonged. It is INTERMITTENT — the same command
  succeeds on the next run — so a green does not clear a captured shim call. Directly measured on
  the shim: the default reporter yields `{"type":"message",…}` on stdout, `PROTO_REPORTER=text`
  yields none. Every gate script that captures shim output therefore **exports
  `PROTO_REPORTER=text` once at the top** (`ci/actionlint/`, `ci/ruff/`, `ci/release-plan/`,
  `ci/release-parity/`), rather than prefixing each call site, so a future capture inherits it.
  The two binary resolvers additionally pipe through `tail -n1`; note that alone is NOT
  sufficient — on the multi-line NDJSON error the last line is still JSON, and what preserves
  fail-closed there is the `[ -x ]` assertion, not the tail.
  **Scope, corrected.** Only `repo:release-parity` was ever affected — NOT all three.
  `ci/release-parity/run.sh` sources exactly ONE ecosystem module per invocation, and only
  `release-plz.sh` invoked the proto CLI; `-py` resolves through `uv run` and `-ts` through `node`,
  and both were measured green in the same agent session that showed `release-parity` aborting.
  The earlier claim here that all three abort was a regression against SMA-530's own spec, which
  had the scope right. The `unset AI_AGENT CLAUDECODE CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` workaround is **no
  longer needed for these gates**; it may still matter for other proto oddities (see the entry
  above). **Residual:** nothing gates this. A new captured proto call written the broken way reds
  nothing (SMA-596 D4) — this bullet is the only control.
  Both ecosystem modules now resolve their tool with **no fallback** and assert `[ -x ]`, exiting 2
  with the harness's own `infrastructure error (rc=2)` classifier in the message — the module is
  sourced by `run.sh`, so an exit fires during the source and `run.sh` never reaches its own abort
  lines. That classifier is what keeps such a failure greppable.
- `repo:affected-smoke` has aborted **twice**, both times under a concurrent `moon ci` on 2.5.3,
  at ~2.4s against its usual 6–8s: once on SMA-595, which captured no output, and once on
  SMA-592, which captured its output. The two are matched on SYMPTOM SHAPE alone — a sub-3s abort
  under a concurrent `moon ci` — so nothing proves they are one and the same failure. Neither
  session reproduced it: four attempts on SMA-595 (warm, cold `.moon/cache`, cold `MOON_HOME`, and
  cold `rs/target` with cargo compiling alongside), and three more on SMA-592. An inherited
  `MOON_BASE` was tested and ruled out (the gate passes with it set). The gate is otherwise green
  everywhere. If you see a sub-3s `affected-smoke` failure, capture the full task output before
  re-running, because a re-run passes and destroys the evidence.
  (SMA-597 measured the mechanism: it is OVERWRITE, not discard. A passing re-run rewrites
  `stdout.log`, truncates `stderr.log`, rewrites `lastRun.json` and flips the `ciReport.json` row
  to `passed`. See the diagnosis procedure entry below.)
  **The mechanism below is measured on the ONE session that captured output (SMA-592), not on
  both.** In that occurrence the failure is an infrastructure ABORT, not a red verdict: the gate's
  own nested `moon query projects` dies with `Error: proto-shim:
  Failed to execute proto for the shimmed command: Permission denied (os error 13)`, writes
  nothing to stdout, and the reader then raises `JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column
  1`, so `run.sh` prints `FATAL [contracts->proto]: moon query failed` and
  `== affected-graph guard ABORTED: infrastructure error (rc=2) ==`. So the proximate cause THERE
  is the **proto shim failing to exec `proto` with EACCES** while a `moon ci` runs concurrently —
  why the shim is briefly non-executable is still unknown, and SMA-595's four hypotheses above
  stay ruled out.
  Two consequences. The gate FAILS SAFE — rc=2 is distinct from rc=1, and it never reports a false
  green. And the `proto-shim` line is the tell, so grep the captured output for it: if that line
  is there, the failure is not about the affected graph at all, and re-running the task alone
  (`moon run repo:affected-smoke --force`) passes in the usual 6s. If it is absent, this entry
  does not explain your failure — diagnose it on its own terms.
  The NDJSON entry above is the same root tool, a different symptom; both mean a `moon`/`proto`
  call inside a gate is the fragile part of an agent-driven local run, never in CI.
- **Diagnosing an unattributed `moon ci` failure.** The procedure below is MEASURED on moon 2.5.3
  (SMA-597); re-take it on a bump. It is for **local** runs — in CI see the note at the end.
  <!-- moon-diagnosis:begin -->
  **Step 0 — capture before you re-run anything.** A re-run overwrites every artifact holding the
  evidence, and a PASSING re-run is just as destructive as another failing one: it rewrites
  `stdout.log`, truncates `stderr.log` to zero bytes, rewrites `lastRun.json`, and flips the
  action to `passed` in `ciReport.json` (all four measured). Copy `.moon/cache/ciReport.json` and
  `.moon/cache/states/<project>/<task>/` somewhere outside the repo first.

  **Step 1 — which task, what command, what exit code.**
  ```bash
  jq '.actions[] | select(.status=="failed")
      | {label, error,
         exec: (.operations[] | select(.meta.type=="task-execution") | {command, exitCode})}' \
     .moon/cache/ciReport.json
  ```
  There is **no action-level `exitCode` key** — `has("exitCode")` is `false`. The widely copied
  query projects `{label, status, exitCode}` and so reports `null` for a key moon never writes,
  which is why this file has a reputation for being empty. It is not: the real exit code and the
  full command are in `operations[]`, on the entry whose `meta.type` is `task-execution`.

  **Step 2 — why.** `cat .moon/cache/states/<project>/<task>/stdout.log` and `stderr.log`. This is
  the only place task output exists. It works for a task that never started: a missing binary
  leaves `stdout.log` empty and `stderr.log` holding `command not found` (exit 127).

  **Step 2a — prove the logs belong to this run. Mandatory.** Compare the report action's
  `finishedAt` against `lastRun.json`'s `lastRunTime`. **If they disagree, stop** — the logs are
  from a different run and pairing them with step 1's command yields a confident wrong answer.
  Two measured causes: `moon run` writes `runReport.json` and does NOT touch `ciReport.json`, so a
  `moon run` re-run desynchronises them; and a cache HIT rewrites neither, so a log can be
  arbitrarily older than the run you are looking at.

  **Step 3 — if it still does not reproduce.** `moon run <target> --force`. Note that
  `buffer-only-failure` prints a FAILING task's output but discards a PASSING one's, and that this
  re-run desynchronises the report and the logs per step 2a.

  **What cannot work:** no `--summary` level (`none`/`minimal`/`normal`/`detailed`) and no
  `outputStyle` (`stream`/`buffer`/`none`) puts stdout or stderr into `ciReport.json`; all seven
  cells are byte-identical, and a key walk over the whole failing action finds no output field at
  any depth. `--log-file` captures moon's own tracing, not a task's stdio. Do not re-litigate this.

  **In CI this procedure does not apply as written.** There is no shell and the runner is
  destroyed, so step 0 is unexecutable; and `ci.yml` restores `.moon/cache` across runs, so a
  cache-hit task's logs may be from an older commit entirely. Use the `moon-diagnostics` artifact
  that `ci.yml` uploads on failure.
  <!-- moon-diagnosis:end -->

## Project shape & process

- [Frontend architecture scoped in Notion](paigasus-frontend-architecture-scoped.md) — multi-zone BFF console lives in Notion, NOT the repo; ADR-0017–0021 Accepted and Better Auth rejected, don't re-litigate; the ADR index table has no gate and drifts

- [main strict checks × dependabot](paigasus-main-strict-checks-dependabot.md) — main needs `moon ci` with strict up-to-date branches, so sequential merges block the next PR; use the update-branch API once you've pushed to a dependabot branch

## Agents, sessions & worktrees

- [Concurrent session branch clash](paigasus-concurrent-session-branch-clash.md) — two sessions in one checkout interleave commits silently; detect with ListAgents, isolate with a worktree, never `checkout`/`branch -f` under a busy peer
- [Subagent worktree pinned cwd](subagent-worktree-pinned-cwd.md) — subagents run pinned to the MAIN checkout; their first action must be EnterWorktree + a branch check, or they commit to local main
- [Subagent background-job stalls](subagent-background-job-stalls.md) — implementers spawn a background job then end their turn waiting on it; dispatch foreground-only and verify with `git log` rather than trusting the report
- [EnterWorktree branch rename](enterworktree-branch-rename.md) — it mints `worktree-<name>`; rename to `feature/sma-NNN-<slug>` before the first commit or Linear auto-link breaks
- [Worktree sandbox: use a script file](worktree-sandbox-script-file-workaround.md) — in a worktree session the sandbox refuses gh/git loops, variables, awk and the perl alarm wrapper; run `/bin/bash <literal scratchpad script>` instead
- [ExitWorktree leaves the local branch](exitworktree-leaves-local-branch.md) — "discarded N commits" still leaves the branch; finish with `git branch -D`, and check `git worktree list` for peers first

## Review tooling (CodeRabbit)

- [CodeRabbit `review` is incremental](coderabbit-review-is-incremental.md) — zero threads means "nothing new", not "clean"; only `full review` forces a real pass. **How to tell all four zero-thread states apart** — including a clean pass that files NO review object, and why the refusal's BODY not its latency is the discriminator
- [CodeRabbit-loop in-progress detector](coderabbit-loop-inprogress-detector.md) — the skill's "come back in a few minutes" grep misses CR's other in-progress wordings; nitpicks hide in the review BODY, not reviewThreads
- [CodeRabbit rate-limit re-trigger is futile](coderabbit-rate-limit-retrigger-futile.md) — a Fair-Usage refusal is a ~393-byte body arriving as an ISSUE COMMENT; only a new push or billing gets a review
- [CodeRabbit CLI last-commit gap](coderabbit-cli-last-commit-gap.md) — a 2-pass local review never covers the fix commit it produced; one more pass found five further findings

## Gate design & proving assertions bite

- [Fixtures inherit the implementer's assumption](fixtures-inherit-the-implementer-assumption.md) — nine review passes missed a case-sensitive `content-type` check because every fixture used lowercase; vary externally-supplied strings by case, parameters and whitespace
- [Fix scope hides the same defect](fix-scope-hides-the-same-defect.md) — one bug survived three plausible scopes ("no chain here", "fix what the review named", "change nothing beyond this file"); put the rule on the helper's contract, then audit every call site
- [Guard-the-guard: pin production call sites](guard-the-guard-production-call-sites.md) — a check's own CALL SITE is what goes unguarded; fixture tables exercise the verdict function, never its invocation
- [Prometheus `# TYPE` vacuous assertions](prometheus-type-line-vacuous-assertion.md) — `contains()` on a TYPE line passes with the increment DELETED; parse a number instead. Also: a metric's prose lives in 3 unlinked places
- [Prometheus new-counter first-sample trap](prometheus-new-counter-first-sample-trap.md) — a series appears already at 1, so `increase()` can never fire on the first occurrence; prime at zero
- [promtool gate semantics](promtool-gate-semantics.md) — `check config` reads ZERO rule files, so it proves nothing about rules loading; always add a control series
- [errexit swallows nested exit codes](errexit-swallows-nested-exit-codes.md) — `foo || ec=$?` cannot see an `exit 2` raised inside a `$( )`, so a rc1-vs-rc2 negative control is silently inoperative
- [Mutation restore discards the fix](mutation-restore-discards-the-fix.md) — `git checkout --` also reverts the UNCOMMITTED fix under test; restore by deleting a marked insert
- [Re-run a mutation battery whole](mutation-battery-rerun-whole.md) — after any fix re-run every mutation; a fixture in a COMMENT went inert when a later fix stripped comments. Time out the harness
- [BSD vs GNU grep on directories](bsd-gnu-grep-directory-divergence.md) — a directory passed to `grep -c` is not a portable read failure: BSD errors, GNU prints `0`; passes on macOS, reds Linux CI
- [repo gates: dependency waivers](paigasus-repo-gates-vs-per-project-tasks.md) — new deps may need a deny.toml exception, a dev-only advisory ignore, or a temporary cargo-machete allowlist
- [repo:redis-connect-single-site gate](paigasus-redis-connect-single-site-gate.md) — bans raw redis constructors in src/ AND tests/; integration tests must exec redis-cli in the container
- [actionlint check 9 control flake](actionlint-check9-control-flake.md) — the control runs the WHOLE gate, so rule out an ordinary check failure on your own branch first; the genuine flake is narrower and its mechanism is still UNKNOWN
- [Gate failures from the wrong bash](gate-failures-from-wrong-bash.md) — a wall of "expected rc 0" self-test failures across unrelated gates means `/bin/bash` 3.2 ran them, not a real finding; check `which -a bash` first (SMA-628)

## Moon & the affected graph

- [moon ci affected model](moon-ci-affected-model.md) — changed-files-only by default; downstream needs `--include-relations` + task-level `^:build`. Dirs with no moon.yml belong only to root `repo`
- [Moon task inputs affect without a project edge](moon-task-inputs-affect-without-project-edge.md) — a workspace-relative input makes the TASK affected while `query projects` still reports only `repo`; treat an absent `inputFiles` key as a violation
- [Moon project id stack suffix](moon-project-id-stack-suffix.md) — ids collide across stacks; suffix `-py` / `-rs`
- [Moon layer field not type](moon-layer-field-not-type.md) — the project field is `layer:`, not `type:`
- [Moon/proto PATH in non-interactive shells](moon-proto-path-noninteractive.md) — shims FIRST or you get the global pin; the Bash tool runs zsh, and macOS has no `timeout`
- [moon .prototools runtime tool pins](moon-prototools-runtime-tool-pins.md) — pin node/pnpm/uv in `.prototools`, not only `.moon/toolchains.yml`, or fresh CI fails `proto::detect::failed`
- [proto-pin cargo CLIs](proto-pin-cargo-clis.md) — add cargo-deny/machete-style gates via a proto plugin, not `rust.bins`; host on root `repo`, toolchain:system
- [proto TOML schema arch is global-only](proto-toml-schema-arch-global-only.md) — vendored plugin TOMLs remap `{arch}` globally only; the per-OS fix is upstream
- [proto does not shim npm](proto-does-not-shim-npm.md) — `~/.proto/shims/` has `node` but NOT `npm`, so a bare `npm` in CI is the runner image's

## Build, CI & platform traps

- [node-redis command vs socket timeout](node-redis-command-vs-socket-timeout.md) — `commandOptions.timeout` bounds only the QUEUED phase; `socket.socketTimeout` is the end-to-end deadline. `@paigasus/auth` still omits it, with a test that pins the incomplete set

- [macOS bash 5.3.15 here-string deadlock](macos-bash-535-herestring-deadlock.md) — THIS machine hangs forever on `while read` fed by a `<<<` over ~512 bytes; hangs `affected-smoke`/`actionlint` locally while CI stays green. Never read the hang as a gate failure
- [affected-smoke hang: use /bin/bash](affected-smoke-hang-fixed-by-system-bash.md) — the deadlock is bash-5.3.15-specific; macOS's system bash 3.2 runs the whole affected-graph suite green in under a minute
- [CI disk exhaustion from large Rust deps](paigasus-ci-disk-large-rust-deps.md) — big dep trees overflow the ~14GB runner disk mid-link; fix with CI-only `line-tables-only` debug + a versioned cache key
- [actions/cache skips save on exact key hit](actions-cache-key-hit-skips-save.md) — widening a cached job without changing the key means the output is never saved, and the verification run hides it
- [Cargo stale build after a restore](cargo-stale-build-after-restore.md) — `mv file.bak file` rolls mtime BACKWARDS so cargo reuses the binary built from your temporary edit; `touch` or revert via Edit
- [Rust fmt drift after an identifier rename](rust-fmt-drift-after-identifier-rename.md) — a longer identifier reflows past max_width; clippy stays clean and `cargo fmt --check` reds
- [Rust workspace warnings=deny staging trap](rust-workspace-warnings-deny-staging-trap.md) — dead code is a hard COMPILE error, so "add now, wire later" plan staging breaks the package
- [ts:fmt Prettier gate is separate](paigasus-ts-fmt-prettier-gate.md) — its own whole-tree CI gate, decoupled from `ts:lint`/tsc; run it after touching any ts file
- [pnpm minimum-release-age](pnpm-minimum-release-age.md) — pnpm 11's 24h default fails CI on same-day npm releases

## Dependabot & lockfiles

- [dependabot cargo lockfile truncation](dependabot-cargo-lockfile-truncation.md) — **SOLVED (SMA-604)**: `members = ["crates/*/*"]` resolved to ZERO members. Keeps the repair recipes and the "moon ci green is NOT proof" warning
- [dependabot pnpm catalog corruption](dependabot-pnpm-catalog-corruption.md) — npm PRs drop a package from `catalogs.default` and rewrite its specifier off `catalog:`; hides behind the release-age check
- [dependency-graph uv-member warnings](paigasus-dependency-graph-uv-member-warnings.md) — benign: auto-discovered graph jobs failing to resolve uv workspace members standalone
- [uv constraint for a transitive CVE](uv-constraint-for-transitive-cve.md) — a group bump can DOWNGRADE a transitive dep into a CVE; use `[tool.uv] constraint-dependencies`, never an osv waiver

## Contracts, FFI & codegen

- [proto buf-format + moon ci silent-fail diagnosis](paigasus-proto-buf-format-ci-diagnosis.md) — editing a `.proto` needs `buf format -w` or `contracts:fmt` reds SILENTLY; `contracts:generate` can serve STALE cache
- [FFI binding pattern (maturin + napi + wasm)](paigasus-uv-maturin-binding-pattern.md) — the three-binding layout plus freshness traps; wasm-pack destructively cleans `--out-dir`; vitest forces the `node` condition
- [kernel FFI surface gotchas](paigasus-kernel-ffi-surface.md) — doc comments churn committed glue; use f64 not u64 at the boundary; uuid pulls getrandom and breaks wasm
- [proto codegen toolchain pins](proto-codegen-toolchain-pins.md) — prost/tonic 0.14, protobuf-es 2.12; betterproto2 has no BSR remote plugin, so a local uv plugin
- [uv_build license-files gotcha](paigasus-uv-build-license-files.md) — uv_build doesn't auto-glob license files, so a PyPI wheel ships no licence text

## Release & publishing

- [crates.io Trusted Publishing needs an existing crate](cratesio-trusted-publishing-needs-existing-crate.md) — a trusted publisher can only be created AFTER a manual first publish, so an OIDC-only job cannot do a first publish. npm same; PyPI differs
- [cargo publish embeds .cargo_vcs_info.json](cargo-publish-vcs-info-seed.md) — from ANY git tree, and `--allow-dirty` keeps it; release-plz reads that sha1 as its changelog boundary

## Async & runtime

- [tokio select! poll-arm starvation](tokio-select-poll-arm-starvation.md) — a relative `sleep` rebuilt inside `select!` restarts on every other arm firing; use an absolute deadline, and order the arms
- [Docker-gated suites silently skip](paigasus-docker-gated-suites-silent-skip.md) — the suites are genuinely FLAKY under parallel load; baseline on unmodified origin/main before blaming your diff

5	language: 'typescript'

8	# --affected` follows; task `inputs` are the ONLY thing that confers affectedness on a DOWNSTREAM;
9	# and a task-level `deps` entry is the ONLY thing that ORDERS this package's tasks after the
10	# generator that writes the tree they read. MEASURED with `moon action-graph
11	# paigasus-discovery-ts:build --dot`: before the `deps` lines below, the graph held
12	# SyncProject(contracts) but NO RunTask(contracts:generate) node at all — `dependsOn` schedules a
13	# project SYNC, never an upstream TASK.
14	dependsOn: ['paigasus-proto-ts']
15	
16	tasks:
17	  # Every task below reads ts/packages/paigasus-proto/src/generated/**, so every one carries
18	  # `deps: ['contracts:generate']`. This is an ORDERING requirement, not an affectedness one, and
19	  # the `inputs` lines cannot supply it. contracts:generate runs `buf generate` with
20	  # `clean: true`, which DELETES that whole tree before rewriting it, and google/rpc/ is only
21	  # restored by the second template at the very end of the ~11s run. Without these lines Moon
22	  # schedules a reader concurrently with the wipe and it compiles a half-deleted tree.
23	  #
24	  # MEASURED in CI (run 34707777645): contracts:generate executed 17:19:56.257-17:20:07.073, and
25	  # paigasus-discovery-ts:build started at 17:20:03.496 — 3.6s inside that window — and died with
26	  # `TS2307: Cannot find module './generated/google/rpc/error_details_pb'`. paigasus-sdk-ts:build
27	  # started 2.2s AFTER the generator finished and passed. The difference was scheduling luck.
28	  # This only surfaced now because contracts:generate is normally a cache HIT; this branch edited
29	  # buf.gen.yaml, so it re-ran for the first time alongside these readers.
30	  #
31	  # APPEND, never `options.merge: replace`. The inherited definitions in
32	  # .moon/tasks/typescript-project.yml supply @group(sources), @group(tests), tsconfig.json,
33	  # package.json, /ts/tsconfig.base.json and /ts/pnpm-lock.yaml; replacing would silently drop all
34	  # of them — the defect SMA-503 fixed on iam-console-ts:build.
35	  build:
36	    deps: ['contracts:generate']
37	    inputs:
38	      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-proto/src/**/*'
39	  typecheck:
40	    deps: ['contracts:generate']
41	    inputs:
42	      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-proto/src/**/*'
43	  test:
44	    deps: ['contracts:generate']
45	    # vitest.config.ts matches neither src/**/* nor tests/**/*, so without this line an edit to the
46	    # `server-only` alias or the resolution conditions serves a cached PASS — and that alias is the
47	    # only thing keeping server-only's unconditional throw from failing the whole suite.
48	    #
49	    # 'README.md' is also required: tests/cosmetic.test.ts reads it and asserts AC4's cosmetic /
50	    # not-a-security-boundary wording, and neither src/**/* nor tests/**/* covers a root-level file
51	    # — without this, deleting that sentence changes no declared input and serves a cached PASS.
52	    inputs:
53	      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-proto/src/**/*'
54	      - 'vitest.config.ts'
55	      - 'README.md'
56	  test-e2e:
57	    # `script` (not `command`): Moon's `command` setting rejects shell syntax outright.
58	    # `set -euo pipefail` mirrors every other `script:` task here — Moon does not enable errexit
59	    # for script blocks on its own. The Playwright spec runs AFTER the vitest containers, under
60	    # the same `set -euo pipefail` (SMA-509): a real Chromium proving the hit-testing property
61	    # jsdom cannot model — see tests/browser/capability-hit-test.spec.ts's header.
62	    script: |
63	      set -euo pipefail
64	      pnpm exec vitest run --config vitest.containers.config.ts
65	      pnpm exec playwright test
66	    # This tier reads the generated tree at RUNTIME rather than through tsc: src/core/state.ts and
67	    # src/types.ts import `@paigasus/proto`, whose index.ts re-exports
68	    # ./generated/google/rpc/error_details_pb, so loading the barrel loads that file. It needs the
69	    # same ordering as the tsc tasks above. In the CI run it started 17:19:56.428, also inside the
70	    # wipe window, and passed only because the modules it happened to load first were already
71	    # rewritten.
72	    deps: ['contracts:generate']
73	    inputs:
74	      - '@group(sources)'
75	      - '@group(tests)'
76	      - 'vitest.config.ts'
77	      - 'vitest.containers.config.ts'
78	      - 'playwright.config.ts'
79	      - 'package.json'
80	      - '/ts/pnpm-lock.yaml'

82	      # Real containers, real Chromium. A cached PASS would replay a green that tested nothing.
83	      cache: false

id: 'iam-console-ts'
layer: 'application'
language: 'typescript'

# Graph documentation, and what `moon query projects --affected` follows. This confers NO
# affectedness on its own: dependsOn schedules an upstream and never selects a downstream
# (CLAUDE.md, Moon 2.5.3). The task `inputs` below are what make these tasks affected by a
# change inside a package. Every package this app compiles is listed, so the `contracts->proto`
# case in ci/affected-graph/run.sh reaches this project (SMA-511 spec § 8).
#
# It confers no ORDERING on a task either, which is a third distinct thing. MEASURED with
# `moon action-graph iam-console-ts:build --dot`: the entry below produced SyncProject(contracts)
# and no RunTask(contracts:generate) node, so every task that reads
# ts/packages/paigasus-proto/src/generated/** carries its own `deps: ['contracts:generate']`
# below. That tree is wiped by `clean: true` at the start of the generator's ~11s run and
# google/rpc/ is only restored at the end of it — see ts/packages/paigasus-discovery/moon.yml for
# the CI measurement of a reader that was scheduled inside that window and failed.
dependsOn:
  - 'paigasus-next-config-ts'
  - 'paigasus-ui-ts'
  - 'paigasus-auth-ts'
  - 'paigasus-sdk-ts'
  - 'paigasus-discovery-ts'
  - 'paigasus-app-shell-ts'
  - 'paigasus-proto-ts'
  - 'paigasus-console-core-ts'

# this app has no src/ — its code is in app/. MEASURED before this fix with
# `moon query projects --id iam-console-ts`: the resolved group was exactly
# ts/apps/iam-console/src/**/*, matching nothing, so editing app/page.tsx selected NO
# console task at all. repo:input-liveness cannot see this — ci/affected-graph/task_inputs.py
# keys its scan to the `repo` project by exact id. (SMA-503 spec §11.1)

# SMA-502 worked around the same hole from the other side, by listing `app/**/*` in each task's
# inputs directly. Both are kept: the group is the real fix, the explicit entries are belt and
# braces if the group is ever removed. Moon MERGES a project's file groups with the inherited
# ones rather than overriding them (measured, SMA-503 M3), so `@group(sources)` now resolves to
# src/**/* plus app/**/*.

    - 'app/**/*'
    # SMA-511: the composition root. Without this, an edit in lib/ serves a cached build and test.
    - 'lib/**/*'

    # createNextConfig() returns shows `output: 'standalone'` is SET; it cannot show Next HONOURED

    # `next build` compiles @paigasus/proto's generated tree through @paigasus/sdk and
    # @paigasus/discovery, so this task must not run while the generator is wiping it.

    # NOTE the `merge: replace` below: this task inherits NOTHING, so every input it needs is
    # listed here. That is how it lost /ts/pnpm-lock.yaml once before — see the comment on
    # repo:next-env-drift in the root moon.yml.

      - '@group(sources)'
      - 'app/**/*'

      # entries keep the coverage if the group is ever removed.
      - 'lib/**/*'

      # unchanged, Moon serves a cached .next, `next build` never runs, and the assertion in
      # `test` passes against stale CSS — a green that means nothing.
      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-ui/src/**/*'
      # The package MANIFEST, not only its sources. It holds the `exports` map — including the
      # ./styles.css entry this app imports — so changing that map must re-key this task
      # (SMA-503 local review, finding A).
      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-ui/package.json'
      # SMA-502 deliberately left the lockfile OFF this task, on the grounds that
      # repo:next-env-drift keys on it instead. SMA-503 adds it back, and the two positions do

      # output is what the Tailwind guard asserts against. The Tailwind, PostCSS and Next
      # versions all come from here, so a bump that changes emitted CSS must rebuild before the

      - 'vitest.config.ts'
      - 'playwright.config.ts'

      - '!tests/fixtures/**/.next/**'
      - '!tests/fixtures/*/next-env.d.ts'
      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-next-config/src/**/*'
      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-next-config/package.json'
      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-next-config/tsconfig.app.json'
      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-ui/src/**/*'

      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-auth/src/**/*'
      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-auth/package.json'
      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-discovery/src/**/*'

      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-next-config/package.json'
      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-next-config/tsconfig.app.json'
      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-ui/src/**/*'

      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-auth/package.json'
      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-discovery/src/**/*'
      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-discovery/package.json'
      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-proto/src/**/*'
      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-proto/package.json'
      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-app-shell/src/**/*'
      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-app-shell/package.json'
      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-sdk/src/**/*'
      - '/ts/packages/paigasus-sdk/package.json'
